:::{#exm-entropy-at-most-log-values}
#### A fair coin and a loaded coin
<!-- no-figure: the example compares two numbers, with nothing to plot -->

A coin toss $X$ has $k = 2$ values, so @thm-entropy-at-most-log-values gives $\entropyf{X} \le \log_2 2 = 1$ [bit](#def-bit).

- A fair coin is [uniform](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-uniform) on its two values,
  so its [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) equals $\log_2 2 = 1$ bit.
- A coin that lands heads with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/4$
  has entropy below $1$ bit:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \entropyf{X}
  &= -\tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{3}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{3}{4} \\
  &\approx 0.500 + 0.311 \\
  &\approx 0.811 \text{ bits}.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

:::
